note: Re-judged 2026-11-02 by an independent auditor who authored none of the change, after a965ee38fb moved community stripping into chain members. RFC 9012 Section 11: "Any BGP speaker that understands it MUST be able to filter it from incoming BGP UPDATE messages." TestRFC9012ConfiguredEncapsulationECIngress now configures the real bgp-filter-community plugin over an RPC pipe, names bgp-filter-community:ingress in the peer's import chain (the member checkCommunityMembers requires), and gives the source an import policy compiled by policychain.Compile with WithLibrary, the same calls bgp/config compileLibraryChain makes for a configured peer. The reactor's peer-chain step sends each route through filter-update to evaluateCommunityFilter, which answers the ingress member with ingressFilter -> applyIngressFilter -> ingressStripCommunities. Every assertion is byte-identical: the remove case requires the Extended Communities attribute to hold only the RT (both 030c000000000002 and 030c000000000008 gone) at receive dispatch, on the forwarded socket bytes and after downstream receipt, with ORIGIN, AS_PATH, NEXT_HOP and NLRI unchanged; the preserve case (populated no-match strip) requires both Encapsulation ECs kept. The two removed require.Len(orderedIngressSteps, 1) lines counted a filterapi registration that no longer exists, so they proved nothing about filtering. The discrimination record, re-taken in 5a77ebfd7e, observed both polarities red with ingressStripCommunities disabled. This proves configurable ingress filtering, not a default-EBGP behaviour.
